reason: The main entry calls receiveWithCheckpanic, whose essential behavior requires named workers, inter-worker receive and send, and propagation of a worker-returned error through checkpanic and wait. Named worker declarations and worker communication are not covered by the supported positive lists; start/wait support alone does not cover them. The whole source also calls unsupported future.cancel().
unsupported_constructs: Named worker declarations and asynchronous/synchronous worker message passing (->, ->>, <-), including error/panic propagation across workers.
test_design_notes: Mixed scope: the source retains many unrelated worker, query, lock and future tests although main only calls receiveWithCheckpanic().

The @panic marker is on the error construction in worker w1, which returns that error; the actual panic is triggered by checkpanic in worker w2 and observed through wait. No @args or @output markers appear.
